title: ECDIS and Electronic Navigation
description: Test your understanding of ECDIS, electronic navigational charts, safety settings, route planning, route monitoring, chart updates, sensor inputs and practical bridge procedures.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of ECDIS onboard a ship?
options: To display electronic chart information together with the vessel's position for route planning and monitoring
To replace all bridge watchkeeping responsibilities
To control the vessel's propulsion and steering systems
To transmit navigational warnings to coastal radio stations
questions.explanation: ECDIS combines official electronic chart information with position and other navigational data to support route planning and route monitoring.

questions.question: What does ENC stand for?
options: Electronic Navigational Chart
Emergency Navigation Control
Electronic Nautical Communication
Enhanced Navigation Calculation
questions.explanation: ENC means Electronic Navigational Chart. It is an official vector chart produced or authorized by a hydrographic office.

questions.question: Which feature shown in the illustration allows the officer of the watch to monitor the vessel's progress along the planned voyage?
options: The planned route with waypoints
The depth legend
The AIS target list
The cursor information panel
questions.explanation: The planned route, shown as a magenta line with waypoints, is used to monitor the vessel's progress during the voyage.

questions.question: Which sensor normally supplies the vessel's geographical position to ECDIS?
options: GNSS or GPS receiver
Gyrocompass
Speed log
Echo sounder
questions.explanation: A GNSS receiver, commonly referred to as GPS, normally provides the vessel's latitude and longitude to ECDIS.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of route monitoring in ECDIS?
options: To compare the vessel's actual movement with the planned route
To create cargo-loading sequences
To calculate engine fuel injection timing
To transmit the voyage plan to nearby vessels
questions.explanation: Route monitoring allows the bridge team to observe the vessel's progress and position relative to the approved route.

questions.question: Why must electronic charts be kept updated?
options: To include the latest navigational changes and safety information
To increase the display brightness
To improve the accuracy of the gyrocompass
To reduce the vessel's fuel consumption
questions.explanation: Chart updates include changes such as new dangers, altered aids to navigation, revised depths and amended restricted areas.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an ENC from an RNC?
options: An ENC contains structured vector data, while an RNC is a digital image of a paper chart
An ENC is unofficial, while an RNC is always official
An ENC can only be used in port, while an RNC is used at sea
An ENC contains radar data, while an RNC contains AIS data
questions.explanation: ENCs are vector databases containing individual chart objects. RNCs are raster images that resemble scanned paper charts.

questions.question: What is the safety contour in ECDIS?
options: A depth contour used to distinguish potentially unsafe water from safer water
The vessel's planned cross-track distance
The maximum permitted speed on the route
A line showing the range of the vessel's radar
questions.explanation: The safety contour is emphasized on the display and is used by ECDIS when warning about entry into potentially unsafe water.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the safety depth setting?
options: To emphasize individual soundings that are equal to or shallower than a selected value
To determine the vessel's minimum engine-room depth
To set the maximum depth displayed on the chart
To calculate the vessel's arrival draft automatically
questions.explanation: Safety depth helps the mariner identify individual depth soundings that may represent insufficient water.

questions.question: Why should a route check be performed after modifying a planned route?
options: To identify dangers, restricted areas and safety-contour crossings along the revised route
To certify that the vessel's engines can maintain the selected speed
To confirm that all crew members have read the voyage plan
To update the vessel's official logbook automatically
questions.explanation: Any route amendment can introduce new hazards. The route should therefore be checked again after changes.

questions.question: What does overscale mean on an ECDIS display?
options: The chart is being displayed at a larger scale than the compilation scale of the available data
The vessel's speed exceeds the value entered in the voyage plan
The selected safety contour is deeper than the vessel's draft
The displayed route contains too many waypoints
questions.explanation: Overscaling enlarges the chart beyond its intended compilation scale and may make the display appear more detailed than the underlying data actually is.

questions.question: Which input is normally provided by the gyrocompass to ECDIS?
options: Heading
Depth below keel
Speed through water
Geographical position
questions.explanation: The gyrocompass normally supplies the vessel's heading.

questions.question: Which input is commonly supplied by the speed log?
options: Speed through the water
Position accuracy
Chart update status
Rate of turn
questions.explanation: A speed log generally supplies speed through the water and may also provide distance travelled.

questions.question: Why is type-specific ECDIS familiarization important?
options: Different manufacturers use different menus, controls, alarm presentations and operating procedures
It replaces the need for general ECDIS training
It allows the officer to modify official ENC data
It removes the requirement for a backup arrangement
questions.explanation: Although ECDIS equipment follows common performance standards, practical operation varies between manufacturers and models.

questions.question: The vessel's calculated safe water requirement is 11 metres, but the ENC contains contours at 10 and 15 metres only. Which contour will ECDIS normally use as the safety contour?
options: The next deeper available contour, 15 metres
The next shallower contour, 10 metres
An automatically created 11-metre contour
The deepest contour visible on the display
questions.explanation: When the exact selected value is unavailable, ECDIS normally uses the next deeper available contour to provide a conservative boundary.

questions.question: The officer enters the vessel's present draft as the safety contour without allowing for squat, under-keel clearance or tidal uncertainty. What is the main risk?
options: The displayed safe-water boundary may not provide sufficient clearance for the vessel
The ECDIS will automatically cancel the voyage plan
The gyrocompass heading will become unreliable
The ENC licence will expire earlier than expected
questions.explanation: Safety settings should reflect the vessel's required safe depth, including draft and all relevant under-keel-clearance allowances.

questions.question: During route planning, the route-check function reports no dangers. The display is heavily filtered and some chart layers are hidden. What should the navigator understand?
options: The route check does not remove the need to inspect the route at appropriate scales and with suitable information displayed
A successful route check proves that the passage is safe under all conditions
Hidden chart objects cannot affect the vessel
The system automatically accounts for every local navigation requirement
questions.explanation: Automated route checking supports, but does not replace, careful visual examination, appropriate display settings and professional judgement.

questions.question: The primary GNSS position suddenly jumps several hundred metres, while radar ranges and visual bearings do not support the new position. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Treat the position as unreliable and verify the vessel's position using independent methods
Alter course immediately to place the ECDIS symbol back on the route
Assume the radar and visual observations are incorrect
Disable all ECDIS alarms and continue monitoring
questions.explanation: Sensor data must be cross-checked. A sudden unexplained position shift may indicate sensor failure, interference or spoofing.

questions.question: The ECDIS position source fails during coastal navigation. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Change to a verified secondary position source and increase position monitoring by independent means
Continue using the frozen last known position
Use AIS targets as the vessel's own position source
Continue without position fixing because the planned route remains displayed
questions.explanation: The bridge team should use an independent backup position source and strengthen monitoring with radar, visual bearings, depth information and other available methods.

questions.question: An officer selects the base display because it appears less cluttered during navigation in confined waters. What is the main danger?
options: Important navigational information not included in the base display may be hidden
The vessel's position will no longer be updated
The safety contour will be deleted from the ENC
The radar overlay will automatically become the primary chart
questions.explanation: The base display contains only a minimum set of information. Other safety-relevant objects may need to be selected and displayed.

questions.question: The bridge team observes that the radar overlay is consistently offset from charted coastlines and buoys. What should this indicate?
options: A possible position, heading, radar-alignment or chart-reference error requiring investigation
Proof that all charted objects are incorrectly surveyed
A normal condition caused by using vector charts
A requirement to increase the safety depth
questions.explanation: A consistent radar-overlay mismatch may reveal errors in sensor inputs, alignment, position or chart datum and must be investigated.

questions.question: A planned route passes close to an isolated danger, but the cross-track limit is wider than the available safe-water corridor. What is the principal concern?
options: The vessel could remain within the permitted cross-track limit while entering unsafe water
The ECDIS will automatically reduce the vessel's speed
The ENC will remove the isolated-danger symbol
The route will no longer contain valid waypoints
questions.explanation: Cross-track limits must be appropriate for the available navigable width and should not extend into hazards or unsafe water.

questions.question: The chart status indicates that an ENC permit has expired for part of the upcoming voyage. What should the navigator do before departure?
options: Obtain valid chart coverage or arrange an approved alternative before using the route
Continue because expired permits only affect chart colours
Use the previously displayed chart without checking its status
Replace the ENC with an unofficial internet chart
questions.explanation: The vessel must have valid, appropriate and up-to-date chart coverage for the intended voyage.

questions.question: An ECDIS update report shows that several updates failed to install. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Investigate the failed updates and ensure the affected charts are corrected before relying on them
Ignore the report if the route appears visually unchanged
Delete the affected ENC cells permanently
Continue because chart updates are only required in port
questions.explanation: Failed updates may leave chart information incomplete or outdated. The issue must be resolved or covered by an approved alternative.

questions.question: The vessel is navigating with an RNC because no suitable ENC is available. Which limitation is particularly important?
options: The raster chart does not contain the same object-based intelligence and automated safety checking as an ENC
The vessel's GPS cannot be displayed on an RNC
RNCs cannot show charted depths
RNCs automatically update without official corrections
questions.explanation: An RNC is essentially a digital image, so individual objects cannot be interrogated or assessed in the same way as ENC vector data.

questions.question: The look-ahead alarm repeatedly activates because the predicted vessel movement crosses the safety contour. What should the officer do?
options: Determine whether the route, safety settings, vessel position and manoeuvring situation are safe before taking action
Silence and permanently disable the alarm
Reduce the safety contour until the warning disappears
Assume the alarm is false because the vessel remains on the route line
questions.explanation: A safety-contour warning requires assessment of the actual navigational situation. Settings should not be altered merely to suppress alarms.

questions.question: Why must an ECDIS-equipped vessel have an adequate backup arrangement?
options: To ensure safe navigation can continue if the primary ECDIS fails
To allow the vessel to operate without updated charts
To provide additional AIS transmission capacity
To replace the requirement for bridge watchkeeping
questions.explanation: The backup arrangement must permit safe navigation following failure of the primary ECDIS and may consist of an independent second ECDIS or another approved arrangement.
